ing: about 0.5 g, soaked in warm broth
st: Keep [[4.5 cups]] of broth hot in a pot and crumble the saffron into a ladle of it to steep.
Heat the oil in a wide paella pan or large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and brown it for 6 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and cook 3 minutes, then push everything to the edge and add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the grated tomato and paprika and cook 5 minutes until thick and jammy.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat it. Pour in the hot broth with the saffron and add [[1.5 tsp]] salt, then spread the rice evenly.
Simmer without stirring for 10 minutes. Nestle the mussels in the rice and add the shrimp.
Cook another 8 to 10 minutes until the rice is tender, the shrimp are pink and the mussels have opened. Throw away any that stay shut, and check the chicken has reached 165°F (74°C).
Turn the heat up for the last minute to toast the bottom, then cover the pan with foil and rest for 5 minutes.
Serve straight from the pan with lemon wedges.
Heat the olive oil in a 9-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and onion with [[1 tsp]] salt and cook gently, turning often, for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft but not browned.
Beat the eggs with [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Strain the potatoes and onion, keeping a tablespoon of oil in the pan and saving the rest for another use.
Fold the warm potatoes into the eggs and let stand for 5 minutes.
Reheat the skillet over medium heat, pour in the mixture, and cook 5 minutes until the edges set.
Place a large plate over the pan, flip the tortilla onto it, then slide it back in to cook the other side for 3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and cool for 10 minutes before cutting into wedges. It is best warm or at room temperature.
Soak the bread in a little water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out lightly.
Put the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic and bread in a blender, working in batches if needed.
Blend until completely smooth, about 2 minutes.
With the blender running, stream in the olive oil so the soup turns pale and creamy.
Blend in the vinegar and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Taste and adjust.
Strain through a fine sieve for a silky texture, pressing on the solids.
Chill in the fridge for at least 3 hours so the flavors come together.
Thin with a splash of cold water if too thick, and serve cold with a drizzle of olive oil.
Blend the tomatoes until smooth, then strain out the skins and seeds with a sieve.
Return the juice to the blender and add the bread. Let it soak for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, vinegar and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and blend until completely smooth.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil so the soup turns thick and pale orange.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar.
Chill for at least 3 hours until very cold.
Spoon into bowls or glasses and top with the chopped egg and ham.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve cold.
Rinse the potatoes and boil in salted water for 8 minutes until almost tender. Drain and dry very well.
For the sauce, heat [[1 tbsp]] oil with the garlic over medium heat for 30 seconds.
Stir in the paprika and chili flakes for 20 seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes, vinegar, sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Simmer 15 minutes until thick, then blend smooth if you like.
Heat the remaining oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the potatoes in two batches for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Pile the potatoes onto a plate, spoon the red sauce over them and add a drizzle of mayonnaise.
Pat the shrimp very dry and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat the oil with the garlic and chili in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook gently for 3 minutes until the garlic starts to turn pale golden. Do not let it brown.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in one layer.
Cook for 2 minutes, flip, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until pink and curled.
Add the sherry and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Stir in the parsley and take off the heat. Serve sizzling in the pan with bread to soak up the oil.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat, add the onion, and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the ham and cook for 2 minutes. Sprinkle in [[0.5 cup]] flour and stir for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Pour in the warm milk a little at a time, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is very thick and pulls away from the pan. Season with the nutmeg and salt.
Spread into a shallow dish, cover the surface with plastic wrap, and chill for at least 2 hours until firm.
Scoop out spoonfuls and roll into small logs. Roll in [[0.25 cup]] flour, dip in the egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the bay leaf.
Hold the octopus by the head and dip it into the water 3 times for a few seconds each to curl the tentacles, then lower it in.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides easily into the thickest part.
Remove the octopus and rest it wrapped in foil for 10 minutes. Keep the cooking water.
In the same water, boil the potatoes for 25 minutes until tender, then peel and slice 1/2 inch thick.
Cut the octopus tentacles with scissors into 1/2-inch rounds.
Lay the potatoes on a plate and put the octopus on top.
Sprinkle with the coarse salt and paprika, then drizzle with the olive oil.
Drain the soaked beans and place in a large pot with the pork belly, onion, bay leaf and olive oil.
Cover with cold water by 2 inches and bring slowly to a boil. Skim the foam.
Add a splash of cold water to calm the boil, which keeps the beans from splitting. Repeat twice.
Add the chorizo and morcilla and the saffron. Reduce to a bare simmer.
Cook uncovered for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring gently, until the beans are creamy and tender.
Season with salt near the end, tasting first, since the meats are salty.
Lift out the sausages and pork, slice them, and return them to the pot.
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve in warm bowls.
Bring the water, butter, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Take it off the heat, add all the flour at once, and stir hard until a smooth dough forms.
Return to low heat and stir for 1 minute, then cool 5 minutes. Beat in the egg if using.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star tip.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Pipe 5-inch strips into the oil, cutting with scissors. Fry 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] coating sugar with the cinnamon and roll the hot churros in it.
For the chocolate, whisk the cornstarch into the milk, heat until steaming, add the chocolate and stir over low heat for 4 minutes until thick. Serve for dipping.
Warm [[1.75 cups]] milk with the lemon zest and cinnamon stick over low heat for 10 minutes. Do not let it boil.
Whisk the cornstarch into the remaining [[0.25 cup]] cold milk until smooth.
In a bowl, whisk the yolks and [[0.5 cup]] sugar until pale.
Strain the warm milk into the yolks slowly while whisking, then whisk in the cornstarch mixture.
Pour back into the pot and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 6 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Divide among 6 shallow dishes and cool, then chill for at least 4 hours.
Sprinkle each custard with [[1 tbsp]] sugar in a thin layer.
Caramelize with a kitchen torch until amber and crisp, or put under a very hot broiler for 1 minute. Serve right away.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Place the peppers, tomatoes and garlic on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the peppers are blackened and the tomatoes are soft.
Put the peppers in a bowl and cover for 10 minutes, then peel and seed them. Peel the garlic.
Fry the bread in [[1 tbsp]] of the oil until golden, about 2 minutes per side.
In a food processor, grind the almonds, hazelnuts and bread to coarse crumbs.
Add the peppers, tomatoes, garlic, vinegar, paprika, cayenne and salt, and blend.
With the machine running, pour in the remaining oil until the sauce is thick and slightly rustic.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar. Serve with grilled vegetables, fish or bread.

ing: pasteurized if you prefer, since it is raw
st: Mash the garlic with the salt in a mortar or on a cutting board with the flat of a knife until it forms a smooth paste.
Move the paste to a bowl and whisk in the egg yolk. This recipe uses raw egg, so use fresh or pasteurized eggs.
Whisk constantly and add the oil a few drops at a time until the mixture begins to thicken.
Once it starts to look like mayonnaise, pour the oil in a thin steady stream, whisking all the time.
Whisk in the lemon juice to loosen it and brighten the flavor.
Taste, add more salt or lemon, and chill until ready. Serve with potatoes, fish or vegetables.
Take the cheeses and cured meats out of the fridge 30 minutes before serving. Fat in the jamón and chorizo softens and tastes sweeter at room temperature.
Slice the chorizo into coins about 1/4 inch thick and the salchichón a little thinner. Fan them out in two separate lines on a large board.
Drape the jamón in loose folds in the center of the board. Handle it gently since the slices are thin and tear easily.
Cut the Manchego into thin triangles, keeping the rind on each piece. Slice the goat cheese into rounds and drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Cut the membrillo into small squares and set them next to the Manchego. The sweet quince paste is the traditional partner for the salty sheep cheese.
Fill two small bowls with the olives and the Marcona almonds. Slice the bread and put it in a basket or at the edge of the board. Serve at once.
nt: No cook: slice, fold, arrange; cheeses at room temperature 30 minutes
Best swap: Mahón or aged Gouda for Manchego, and Spanish smoked paprika roasted chickpeas instead of the meats for a vegetarian board.

st: Toast [[2 cups]] flour in a dry pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for about 8 minutes until pale beige and nutty smelling. Do not let it brown. Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 325°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Cream [[0.75 cup]] lard or butter with [[0.75 cup]] powdered sugar until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Mix in the cooled flour, [[0.75 cup]] ground almonds, [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon and a pinch of salt until a crumbly dough forms that holds when squeezed.
Press the dough to 0.75 inch thick and cut rounds with a 2 inch cutter, or roll balls and flatten gently. Place on the sheet.
Bake 20 minutes until set and barely colored. They are very fragile when hot.
Cool on the sheet for 20 minutes, then dust well with powdered sugar. Handle gently.
nt: Flour pan-toasted, then baked at 325°F
Best swap: use butter instead of lard 1:1, or hazelnut flour in place of the almonds.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease an 8 inch springform tin with the butter and line the base with parchment.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 4 minutes with a hand mixer until pale, thick and doubled in volume.
Fold in the ground almonds, lemon zest and cinnamon with a spatula until no dry streaks remain.
Pour the batter into the tin and tap it on the counter twice to pop air bubbles.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then release the ring and cool completely on a rack.
Lay a cross stencil on top, dust with the powdered sugar through a sieve, then lift the stencil away carefully.
nt: Baked at 350°F, flourless
Best swap: sub orange zest for the lemon zest 1 to 1; the cake is already gluten free.

st: Whisk [[2 tbsp]] cornstarch with a splash of cold milk in a small bowl until no lumps remain.
Warm the rest of the [[3 cup]] milk, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and the cinnamon stick in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming. Do not boil.
Add [[5 oz]] chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of salt. Whisk constantly until fully melted and smooth.
Whisk in the cornstarch mixture, then cook over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, whisking, until it is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove the cinnamon stick and pour into small cups. Serve hot with churros or plain biscuits for dipping.
nt: Melted and thickened on the stovetop with cornstarch
Best swap: dairy-free, use oat milk at the same amount; no cornstarch, reduce longer by 5 minutes.

st: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, warm water and [[0.25 cup]] olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then cover and rise in a warm spot for 1 hour.
Cook the onion and peppers in [[0.25 cup]] olive oil over low heat for 25 minutes, until very soft and sweet.
Stir in the tomatoes and paprika and cook 8 minutes until thick. Fold in the tuna and cool.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Divide the dough in two and roll each piece into a large rectangle about 1/8 inch thick.
Lay one sheet on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Spread the filling over it, leaving a 1 inch border, and cover with the second sheet.
Fold and crimp the edges to seal. Cut a small vent hole in the top, brush with beaten egg and bake until golden and crisp, about 35 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice into squares.
nt: Baked at 400°F
Best swap: use cooked cod or chicken in place of tuna, same amount. A sofrito of onion and pepper keeps the filling moist.

st: Toast the almonds on a tray at 350°F until golden, about 10 minutes, then grind in a food processor into a thick paste.
Heat the honey in a heavy pot over low heat for 20 minutes until it darkens slightly and smells toasty. Do not let it boil hard.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved, then cook to 275°F on a candy thermometer.
Whip the pasteurized egg white to stiff peaks. With the mixer running, slowly stream in the hot syrup in a thin line.
Fold in the almond paste and oil, then cook gently over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it pulls from the sides.
Press into a wafer-lined 8 by 4 inch pan, cover with wafer, weigh down with a plate and cool for 12 hours before slicing.
nt: Cooked syrup, no baking after toasting
Best swap: use hazelnuts or pistachios for the same weight, and maple syrup in place of honey for a looser texture.

st: Scrub the scallop shells and discard any that stay open when tapped. Shuck them if needed, keeping the coral. Pat the meat very dry.
Heat a heavy griddle or cast iron pan over high heat for 3 minutes until smoking lightly. Brush it with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Place the scallops in the shell or just the meat on the plancha in one layer. Sear 2 minutes without moving until deeply golden underneath.
Flip and cook 1 minute more. Scallops are done when just opaque and firm to the touch, around 130°F inside.
Move them to a platter. In the same pan, warm [[2 tbsp]] oil and garlic for 30 seconds until pale gold only.
Pour over the garlic oil, then add parsley, the juice of the lemon, paprika and flaky salt. Serve right away.
nt: Seared very hot on a plancha, 3 minutes total
Best swap: use sea scallops, halved, in a hot cast iron pan. Dry well and use 4 minutes total for large ones.

st: Rinse the tiger nuts in cold water, picking out any stones. Cover with water in a bowl and soak 8 hours or overnight until plump.
Drain and rinse again. Place in a blender with [[2 cups]] cold water and blend on high for 2 minutes until a thick, grainy paste forms.
Add [[3 cups]] cold water, the sugar, lemon peel and cinnamon, and stir well. Let it infuse in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Strain through a nut milk bag or fine cloth, squeezing firmly to get all the milk out. Discard the pulp.
Taste, add sugar if needed, and chill until very cold. Stir before serving over ice.
nt: No cook: soak, blend and strain, serve ice cold
Best swap: tiger nuts are hard to find, use 1 cup raw almonds soaked overnight for an almond horchata with a similar milky body.

ing: halved, grated on a box grater
st: Heat a large cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Add [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and the whole peppers in one layer.
Cook 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and darken in spots and the peppers soften. Pile on a plate and sprinkle with the flaky salt.
Toast the baguette slices in the oven at 400°F for 6 to 8 minutes, until crisp at the edges and golden.
Rub each warm toast with a cut garlic clove, then spread with the grated tomato. Drizzle [[2 tbsp]] olive oil over them and add a pinch of salt.
Arrange the ham in loose folds, the cheese, olives and almonds on a board.
Serve everything right away while the peppers are hot and the toast is crisp.
nt: Peppers blistered in a smoking hot skillet, bread toasted in the oven; ham and cheese uncooked
Best swap: shishito peppers for Padron, same weight; skip the ham and use roasted almonds for vegetarian.

st: Make the gildas. Thread on a toothpick one olive, one folded anchovy fillet, one guindilla pepper and a second olive. Make 12 and chill them.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet over high heat. Add the mushrooms in one layer and cook 5 minutes without moving until browned on the bottom.
Add [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and the garlic and toss 1 minute. Add the sherry vinegar, parsley and salt. Take off the heat.
Toast the baguette slices on a sheet pan at 425°F for 5 minutes until golden at the edges.
Spread goat cheese on 9 toasts and top with the garlic mushrooms. Tear the piquillo peppers into strips and drape them over the other 9 toasts after spreading with cheese.
Brush the piquillo toasts with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, spear each with a toothpick and serve with the gildas on one platter.
nt: Mushrooms sauteed hot in a skillet, bread toasted in the oven; gildas are assembled cold
Best swap: pickled jalapeno slices for guindilla peppers, one slice per skewer; skip anchovy for roasted red pepper.

st: Mix the flour, water, yeast, sugar, egg and a pinch of salt. Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest 30 minutes covered.
Divide into 8 balls and rest 15 minutes. Roll each ball into a long thin sheet as thin as you can without tearing.
Spread each sheet generously with softened lard (about [[1 tbsp]] each). Roll up into a rope from the long edge.
Coil each rope into a loose spiral on a greased tray, tuck the end underneath and leave space for rising.
Cover and rise for 2 hours until very puffy. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes until golden. Cool, then dust thickly with [[0.5 cup]] powdered sugar.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use butter or vegetable shortening for the lard at the same quantity, though butter gives a less crisp finish.

st: Heat the oven to 400°F. Warm [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, chorizo and ham and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, tomatoes, peas and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 8 minutes until thickened.
Make four small wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are fully set and the yolks are as firm as you like. Eggs need whites completely opaque for safety.
Rest for 2 minutes and serve straight from the skillet with bread.
nt: Simmered, then baked at 400°F
Best swap: leave out the chorizo and ham and add 1 tsp extra smoked paprika to make it vegetarian.

st: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pierce the eggplants with a fork. Place the eggplants, peppers, onions and garlic on a lined tray.
Roast for 25 minutes. Remove the garlic cloves if soft. Turn the vegetables and roast another 25 minutes until the skins are charred and the flesh is collapsing.
Put the hot peppers in a bowl and cover tightly. Steam for 15 minutes, which loosens the skins.
Peel the skins from everything. Tear the peppers, eggplant and onions into long strips and squeeze the garlic from its skins.
Arrange on a platter, drizzle with [[0.25 cup]] olive oil and [[1 tsp]] vinegar, and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] flaky salt and parsley.
Serve warm or at room temperature, ideally with grilled bread.
nt: Roasted whole at 425°F
Best swap: char over a gas flame or a grill, turning often, instead of the oven for a smokier taste.

st: Tear the bread into pieces and soak it in [[0.5 cup]] of the cold water for 5 minutes until soft. Squeeze out the extra water lightly.
Add the almonds, garlic, soaked bread and salt to a blender. Pour in [[1 cup]] cold water and blend on high for 2 minutes until a thick, grainy paste forms.
With the blender running, drizzle in the olive oil slowly so the soup turns creamy and pale. Blend 1 more minute.
Add the sherry vinegar and the remaining cold water. Blend briefly, then taste and adjust salt and vinegar so it is bright but not sharp.
For a very smooth soup, pour it through a fine sieve, pressing with a spoon. Chill in the fridge until very cold.
Ladle into small bowls, scatter the grape halves on top, and finish with a thin thread of olive oil.
nt: No cook: just blend, served ice cold
Best swap: blanched marcona or raw cashews 1:1 if almonds are unavailable; use day-old baguette for the bread.
